items.passage: "Come up to the bridge at dawn and see the coast," Mai said, as she had said every evening since Otaru. Folasade, found curled behind crates of brass gears bound for a clock-maker's shop in Hakodate, had each time thanked the captain and stayed below, oiling small movements nobody had asked her to touch. On the fourth night the ship's own chronometer stopped, and the mate swore it could not be repaired before port. Folasade had it ticking again within the hour. Mai, taking the mended clock from her hands, made no mention of the bridge and was ______ with her thanks. She nodded once, set a second mug of tea beside the stowaway's tools, and left the cabin door unlatched behind her.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: noticeably cool
warmly insistent
tactfully brief
somewhat hesitant
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Mai는 매일 저녁 초대를 반복했지만, 시계를 고친 뒤에는 초대를 더 꺼내지 않아 상대의 거절을 존중하는 절제를 보인다. 빈칸 뒤에서는 고개를 한 번 끄덕이고 차를 두고 문을 열어 두는 짧지만 따뜻한 행동이 이어진다. 따라서 말은 아끼되 배려가 담긴 C가 두 제약을 모두 만족한다. A는 초대를 멈춘 점만 보고 차갑게 읽은 것이고, B는 앞의 반복 초대에서 빌린 표현이며, D는 말을 아낀 정도를 망설임으로 한 단계 다르게 읽었다.

items.passage: Who taught me patience on a rooftop in Dayton, if not Mabel? Each morning that summer she climbed to the cedar water tank she was rebuilding and laid out the same three planes before touching a single stave, and each morning I, Aoife, her apprentice of nine weeks, was already reaching for the hammer. In July a storm split two staves she had fitted weeks earlier. I expected her to curse; instead she sat on the tar paper and ran a thumb along the break for a long while. When I offered to cut new staves that very afternoon, her reply was ______. She handed me a plane rather than the saw and pointed me toward the first board, the one I had rushed in June and left rough along one edge.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: plainly grateful
patiently approving
visibly shaken
gently deflecting
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Mabel은 매일 도구를 같은 순서로 늘어놓는 신중한 습관을 보이고, 폭풍 뒤에도 서두르지 않는다. 빈칸 뒤에서 그녀는 톱 대신 대패를 건네며 Aoife가 6월에 서둘러 만든 판자로 관심을 돌린다. 따라서 제안을 부드럽게 비켜 가는 D가 앞의 신중함과 뒤의 방향 전환을 모두 만족한다. A와 B는 제안을 받아들였다고 읽어 뒤 행동과 맞지 않고, C는 폭풍 장면에서 빌린 표현이다.

items.passage: Harriet, whose father ran the lake ferry, sold tickets at the Strand each winter, when the films were old and the seats mostly empty. Hollis came every Thursday, paid in exact coins, and took row nine. For six weeks their exchanges never varied: "One, please." "Enjoy the picture." She tore his stub along the perforation, neat as a hem, and he thanked her in the same courteous murmur, and she noted, as she noted everything, that his coat smelled of diesel and lake wind. On the seventh Thursday he laid the coins down and did not pick up the stub. He asked whether her father still ran the early crossing in March. Then he asked about the ice. Then, for a long time, he asked nothing at all and stood looking through the glass. Harriet slid the stub toward him and kept her fingers on it a moment longer than the tear required.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From routine courtesy to mild irritation, as Hollis's questions delay Harriet's careful work at the window
From routine courtesy to tentative closeness, as Hollis's questions draw Harriet past the usual exchange at the window
From routine courtesy to tentative closeness, as Harriet's close attention to Hollis's coat leads him to speak more openly
From warm familiarity to strained formality, as the usual exchange at the window gives way to unfamiliar questions
items.explanation: 전반부는 매주 똑같은 인사와 표를 찢는 정확한 동작으로 정중하지만 틀에 박힌 관계를 보여 준다. 일곱 번째 목요일에 Hollis가 표를 집지 않고 아버지의 배와 얼음에 대해 묻고 침묵하면서 문장의 흐름이 바뀐다. 마지막에 Harriet이 표 위에 손을 더 오래 두는 동작은 그의 질문이 그녀를 평소의 교환 너머로 끌어냈음을 암시하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 변화를 짜증으로 한 단계 다르게 읽었고, C는 변화의 원인을 Harriet 쪽으로 뒤집었으며, D는 겉의 정중함 변화만 보고 방향을 반대로 읽었다.

items.passage: When the orchestra reached the guesthouse in Samarkand, Bahram, its conductor, made a ceremony of the evening rounds. He counted cases, checked that every bow had been loosened, and told each player, in his slow formal Persian, which corridor led to the well. Aydin, the youngest violinist, received the same instructions as the cellists, along with a nod reserved for the section's newest chair. Tonight Aydin held out a folded letter from a conservatory in Vienna. Bahram read it under the lamp. He refolded it along its creases. He asked whether the courtyard pomegranates were ripe yet, and whether Aydin had eaten. Then he went on to the next door and told the oboist about the well, the corridor, the bows, in exactly the order he always had, only more slowly, and twice he stopped to look back down the hall.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From orderly authority to quiet resentment after Bahram reads the letter Aydin hands him
From orderly authority to renewed confidence once Bahram resumes his familiar evening rounds
From orderly authority to subdued reluctance after Bahram reads the letter Aydin hands him
From orderly authority to subdued reluctance after Bahram's questions about the pomegranates go unanswered
items.explanation: 전반부에서 Bahram은 악기와 활을 점검하고 길을 안내하는 의식 같은 순회로 질서 있는 권위를 보인다. Aydin이 빈의 음악원 편지를 건넨 뒤 그는 짧은 문장으로 편지를 접고 엉뚱한 질문을 던지며 화제를 비튼다. 마지막에 같은 순서를 더 느리게 반복하고 두 번 복도를 돌아보는 동작은 떠나보내기 싫은 가라앉은 마음을 암시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 감정의 성격을 분노로 한 단계 강하게 읽었고, B는 유지된 순회 형식만 보고 변화를 놓쳤으며, D는 변화의 원인을 Bahram 자신의 질문으로 돌렸다.

items.passage: Carn Galver's bus shelter stands on the moor road above the sea, and Cyrus and I waited there the morning after our last gig at the Pendeen hall. He was recounting the evening to me, as he always did, set by set: the tuning delay, the broken string in the third number, the man by the bar who had walked out during my solo. He named the chords. He named the order of the songs. He was precise, generous, even funny about the string. I said I remembered the man leaving during his song, not mine. Cyrus looked at the timetable. He said the bus was late. He said the wind had changed. After that he read the timetable aloud, stop by stop, Morvah, St Just, Sennen, until the bus came around the headland, and he let me board first and took the seat across the aisle.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From assured recollection to cheerful distraction as Cyrus turns his attention toward the bus
From assured recollection to guarded withdrawal after Cyrus notices that the bus is running late
From assured recollection to bitter accusation after Leah offers a different account of the evening
From assured recollection to guarded withdrawal after Leah offers a different account of the evening
items.explanation: 전반부에서 Cyrus는 공연을 세트별로 자세하고 너그럽게 회상하며 자신감 있는 어조를 보인다. 화자 Leah가 그 남자가 자기 독주가 아니라 Cyrus의 곡에서 나갔다고 말한 뒤 그의 문장은 짧아지고 화제는 시간표와 바람으로 옮겨 간다. 마지막에 그가 정류장 이름만 읽고 통로 건너편에 앉는 동작은 다른 증언 이후의 방어적 거리 두기를 암시하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 겉의 화제 이동만 보고 쾌활함으로 읽었고, B는 원인을 버스 지연으로 바꿨으며, C는 거리 두기를 비난으로 한 단계 강하게 읽었다.

items.passage: Coconut oil and the hiss of the steriliser filled the barbershop in Kochi where Tara waited each Saturday while her stepson had his hair cut. Arjun, sixteen, kept his eyes on the mirror and never on her. Every week she did the same small thing: she folded a receipt from the cricket academy into a square and tucked it beneath the barber's comb tray. It was from the trial he had missed in March, after she drove him to the wrong ground. Arjun took the folding for a kind of scorekeeping, a record of what she had cost him. This week the barber, tidying, lifted the tray and handed the square to Arjun. Inside, under the date, Tara had written in pencil a list of grounds and coaches and the dates of next season's trials, some crossed out, some circled twice. Arjun turned the paper over. He did not look at her in the mirror. He asked the barber to take a little more off the sides, and he kept the paper on his knee.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a repeated gesture, reveals its meaning through a chance discovery, and ends before Arjun's response is settled
It describes a repeated gesture, explains Arjun's resentment about the trial, and dwells on Tara's mistake in March
It reveals the meaning of a repeated gesture, then shows Arjun gradually forming his first mistaken view of it
It describes a repeated gesture, reveals its meaning, and ends with Arjun forgiving Tara for the missed trial
items.explanation: 글은 이발소의 감각 묘사와 Tara가 매주 영수증을 접어 넣는 반복 동작으로 시작한다. 중간에 이발사가 우연히 종이를 건네면서 그것이 다음 시즌 테스트 일정을 찾아 둔 목록임이 드러나 Arjun의 해석이 뒤집힌다. 끝에서 Arjun은 그녀를 보지 않은 채 종이를 무릎에 두어 반응이 정리되지 않은 채 끝나므로 A가 정답이다. B는 전반부 전개만 요약했고, C는 오해와 재해석의 순서를 뒤집었으며, D는 열린 결말을 화해로 오독했다.

items.passage: We were sheltering in the gymnasium of a Tromsø school because the airport road had closed, and the stranger on the next mat, Saga, spent the first hour taping a frayed ski strap with the care of someone mending a sail. I watched her measure each strip against her thumb before tearing it. When I mentioned, after giving my name as Emil, that I was flying south to accept a scholarship in Delft, she asked what it covered. Tuition, I told her, and a room. She nodded and asked nothing more. Later, when the volunteers brought soup, she gave her bread roll to a boy whose family had none and then rewrapped the strap she had already finished, slowly. I began to notice the patched cuffs of her jacket, the boots resoled more than once. At midnight the road reopened. She wished me luck in Delft and went back to her strap.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It moves from the narrator's account of his scholarship to Saga's open admiration for the opportunity he has
It moves from the narrator's notice of a careful habit to his gradual reading of it as a sign of hardship
It moves from the narrator's sense of Saga's hardship to his gradual notice of a careful habit she keeps
It moves from the narrator's notice of a careful habit to Saga's decision to seek a scholarship of her own
items.explanation: 글은 Saga가 스키 끈을 정성스럽게 테이프로 감는 모습을 Emil이 관찰하는 장면으로 시작한다. 장학금이 무엇을 지원하는지 묻고 더 묻지 않는 대화 뒤, 화자는 덧댄 소매와 여러 번 고친 신발을 알아차리며 그 습관을 형편의 표시로 다시 읽게 된다. 따라서 습관의 관찰에서 그 의미의 재해석으로 이동하는 B가 정답이다. A는 장학금 대화만 구조로 삼았고, C는 관찰과 해석의 순서를 뒤집었으며, D는 열린 결말을 그녀의 결심으로 오독했다.

items.passage: Dwayne, my brother's tutor, rode the night bus out of Dakar's Plateau with me every Thursday after lessons, and every Thursday he wrote the week's vocabulary on the fogged window with one finger, then wiped it clean before my stop. I took it for a teacher's tic. My brother had stopped answering to the name our grandmother gave him the year we moved, and nobody at home used it now. One night Dwayne asked, "Yaa, what does the name on your brother's old exercise book mean?" He had found the book inside a borrowed dictionary. I told him. He was quiet through three stops. Then he wrote on the window, not a vocabulary word but the name, in careful letters, and did not wipe it away. When we reached Grand Yoff he got off without a word about it, and I watched the letters run in the condensation as the bus pulled out.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a habit the narrator dismisses, recalls how a family move changed a name, and dwells on that loss
It presents a question that gives a habit new weight, then shows the narrator first dismissing it as a tic
It presents a habit the narrator dismisses, shows a question that gives it new weight, and closes on an unexplained image
It presents a habit the narrator dismisses, shows a question that changes it, and closes with the old name restored
items.explanation: 글은 Dwayne이 김 서린 창에 단어를 썼다가 지우는 습관과 이를 버릇으로 여기는 Yaa의 판단으로 시작한다. 중간에 그가 동생의 옛 이름의 뜻을 묻는 질문이 나오고, 그 뒤 그는 그 이름을 써 놓고 지우지 않아 습관이 새로운 무게를 얻는다. 글은 글자가 흘러내리는 모습을 설명 없이 보여 주며 끝나므로 C가 정답이다. A는 전반부의 이름 변화만 구조로 요약했고, B는 순서를 뒤집었으며, D는 열린 결말을 이름의 회복으로 오독했다.

items.passage: I had clerked for Judge Eamon for one summer when he invited me to his terrace above the Saône and announced, as if testing the sound of my name, that Takoda and he would finish the Ferrand file that week. __He kept the file's last page face down beneath a stone ashtray, as he had on the bench, where he never read a verdict until he had heard every word.__ We worked through the mornings. He corrected my French, poured the coffee himself, and pointed out which slope of vines belonged to which cousin. By Friday the other pages were annotated in his small slanted hand, and nothing remained to be heard. When I reached for the ashtray, he covered it with his palm, asked about my plans for autumn, and suggested I carry the file back to the court with the last page unread, just as it was.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers background on Eamon's career that explains why Takoda was invited to the terrace
It establishes a habit of patience that the finished annotations show Eamon has now outgrown
It establishes a general principle of fairness that guides how Eamon treats his young clerk
It establishes a habit that later makes Eamon's covering of the page seem like avoidance
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 보면 판사 시절의 신중한 습관을 소개하는 배경 설명처럼 보인다. 중간의 커피와 포도밭 장면을 지나, 금요일에는 들을 것이 더 남지 않았는데도 Eamon은 재떨이를 손으로 덮고 마지막 장을 읽지 않은 채 돌려보내자고 한다. 이 후반 사건 때문에 밑줄 문장은 끝을 마주하기를 피하는 태도의 복선으로 다시 읽히므로 D가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장만 따로 읽었고, B는 기능을 습관의 해소로 뒤집었으며, C는 일반적 원칙으로 넓혀 후반 단서와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Ayita practiced her recital piece in the back room of the post office outside Albuquerque, where their aunt was postmistress and the piano was older than the building. Faris, home from his deployment for three weeks, sorted mail at the counter while she played. __Each time she reached the slow middle section, he set down whatever letter he held and waited, as if listening for a step on the porch.__ She assumed he found that passage dull. On Saturday, the day before the recital, she skipped the slow section to save time and went straight to the bright ending. Faris kept sorting. That evening she found a sheet of paper on the piano bench in his blocky printing: the dates of four letters she had written him overseas, and beside each, the name of the piece she had said she was learning. All four named the same piece. She sat down and began again from the first bar.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It records a habit of Faris's whose meaning becomes clear once Ayita finds the paper he left
It shows Faris's boredom with the music, which explains why he keeps sorting when Ayita skips
It introduces a tension between the siblings that Ayita's choice to skip the section resolves
It describes the hushed mood of the post office that remains typical of the setting throughout
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 느린 부분에서 Faris가 편지를 내려놓고 기다리는 모습을 묘사해, 처음에는 분위기 묘사나 지루함으로 읽힐 수 있다. 후반에 Ayita가 찾은 종이에는 그녀가 해외로 보낸 편지 네 통의 날짜와 모두 같은 곡 이름이 적혀 있어, 그 곡이 그에게 특별했음이 드러난다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 나중에 의미가 밝혀지는 습관을 기록하는 기능을 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 Ayita의 표면적 추측을 따랐고, C는 기능을 갈등의 해소로 뒤집었으며, D는 배경 묘사라는 일반적 기능으로 넓혔다.

items.passage: Menthol and floor wax met me every night I brought my father's dinner to the pharmacy in Valparaíso where he worked the late shift. __My father, Nicolas, kept a jar of hard candies by the register and gave one to every customer who came in after midnight, whether they bought anything or not.__ I helped with the English labels on the tourists' prescriptions, translating dosages while he restocked shelves he had arranged by color rather than by alphabet. One night a nurse from the port hospital came in for gauze, and while I, Renata, rang her up, she watched the doorway. A sailor, then a woman with a sleeping child, then an old man in slippers came in, took a candy, spoke a few words with my father, and left with nothing. The nurse said she had sent half of them here herself, on the nights the clinic was full. My father shrugged and refilled the jar.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It provides background on the pharmacy's routine that explains why Renata helps with the labels
It presents a small courtesy that a visitor's remark later reveals as care others depend on
It introduces a habit of Nicolas's that the nurse's remark shows to be a simple business strategy
It establishes the general warmth of the family that runs through Renata's memories of the city
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 보면 약국의 소소한 일과를 소개하는 배경처럼 보인다. 중간의 라벨 번역 장면을 지나, 간호사가 병원이 붐비는 밤에 사람들을 직접 이곳으로 보냈다고 말하면서 사탕을 주는 습관이 이웃이 기대는 돌봄이었음이 드러난다. 가족은 몰랐던 것을 방문자가 보게 만드는 이 후반 단서 때문에 B가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장만 따로 읽었고, C는 사람들이 아무것도 사지 않는 점과 맞지 않는 상업적 해석이며, D는 가족의 따뜻함이라는 일반적 기능으로 넓혔다.
